name: Existence and Attributes
path: Theology Proper: The Doctrine of God

objectives.text: Identify God as the one true God who made all things
Recall that the things God made show that He is real and great
Name God as all-powerful and give an example of His power from a Bible story
Name God as all-knowing and give an example of something God knows that people cannot
Recall that God is present everywhere at the same time
Describe God as good, loving, and faithful using Bible verses that say so
Explain that God is spirit and does not have a body like ours
Explain that God is eternal, having no beginning and no end
Recite the Westminster Shorter Catechism definition of God and explain each attribute it names in their own words
Compare God's holiness with human sinfulness using Isaiah's vision of God
Classify God's attributes as incommunicable (belonging to God alone) or communicable (reflected in people made in His image) and justify each choice
Explain how creation reveals God's existence and power and why Scripture says this leaves people without excuse
Explain how God's justice and mercy are both fully true of Him using God's self-description to Moses
Describe how God's wisdom is displayed in creation and in redemption
Analyze the aseity of God by explaining what it means that God is self-existent and needs nothing from His creatures
Analyze what Scripture means by God's omnipotence, including why God cannot lie or deny Himself
Interpret the immutability of God, including passages that describe God as relenting
Explain the doctrine of divine simplicity and connect it to the unity of God
Distinguish the biblical teaching of God's infinity and omnipresence from pantheism
Explain the Reformed doctrine of divine impassibility and interpret biblical passages that describe God with human emotions
Explain the incomprehensibility of God and how Scripture's language about God is true though not exhaustive
Evaluate the cosmological, teleological, and moral arguments for God's existence in light of Scripture's teaching on general revelation and human suppression of the truth
Defend the Reformed position that God can be known truly though not fully
Evaluate Open Theism against classical theism using biblical teaching on God's knowledge and immutability
Synthesize the transcendence and immanence of God in a written account that draws on key biblical texts
Construct an integrated account of the divine perfections that shows how God's attributes cohere in His one simple being

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (one true God, power and knowledge, omnipresence, spirit, communicable vs incommunicable, holiness, aseity, immutability, simplicity, impassibility, knowability, Open Theism, transcendence and immanence, divine perfections). Dropped the grade 4 infinite and eternal item and the grade 6 omni-categorizing item as restatements, folding eternity into grade 3 and infinity into a grade 9 objective against pantheism. Added the missing existence strand (creation's witness at grade 1, general revelation at grade 5, theistic arguments at grade 10) and missing attributes (goodness, love, faithfulness, justice and mercy, wisdom, the meaning of omnipotence, incomprehensibility) plus a catechism recitation objective. Split omnipotence and omniscience. Left decrees and the Trinity to sibling sub-topics. Normalized confession names, added Belgic Confession Articles 1 and 2 and WCF 1.1, and gave every objective verse-level anchors.
